title: The staleness users actually notice — and the targeted fix
description: Users have no expectations about the freshness of other people's data. They have absolute expectations about their own. Read-your-own-writes fixes the complaint without paying for global strong consistency.

nodes.label: Cheaper than strong consistency
nodes.sublabel:
Pin a user's reads to the primary
for a few seconds after they write,
or pass a version token so the read
waits for a caught-up replica.

steps.text: The user saves a change. The write goes to the primary and is acknowledged — genuinely durable, genuinely committed.
Their browser immediately reloads. That read is routed to a replica for scale — and the replica has not received the change yet.

The user sees their old profile and concludes the save failed. Nothing is broken: this is asynchronous replication working exactly as designed. It is a design consequence, not a defect — which is why the fix is a design decision rather than a bug fix.
The write is acknowledged as before, and the session records that this user wrote at this moment.
For a short window afterwards, this user's reads bypass the replicas and go to the primary — or carry a version token so they are served only by a replica that has caught up.

Everyone else keeps reading from replicas at full scale. You have bought the one guarantee users can perceive without paying the latency and availability cost of strong consistency everywhere. That selectivity is the whole point.
